column1: saturate§The market is saturated and the price has stopped falling.§市场已经**饱和**，价格不再下跌。
savanna§Savanna gives way to woodland at about eight hundred metres.§**大草原**在大约八百米处让位给林地。
scandalous§What was scandalous in 1890 is unremarkable now.§一八九〇年**可耻的**事，如今平淡无奇。
scapegoat§Finding a scapegoat is faster than finding a cause.§找**替罪羊**比找原因快。
scathing§A scathing note in the margin was signed with one initial.§页边一条**尖刻**的批注只签了一个首字母。
scent§The dog lost the scent at the river and picked it up again.§狗在河边失去了**气味**，后来又找了回来。
scholarly§Scholarly caution reads as evasion to a general audience.§**学者式**的审慎在普通读者看来像是回避。
scoff§Do not scoff at a method until you have run it once.§没跑过一遍之前，别**嘲笑**一种方法。
scope§There is scope for a second edition if anyone funds it.§如果有人资助，还有出第二版的**余地**。
scorn§Scorn is the cheapest response and the least informative.§**轻蔑**是最廉价、也最没有信息量的反应。
scour§Wind scoured the ridge down to bare rock.§风把山脊**冲刷**得只剩裸岩。
scrupulous§Scrupulous about attribution, he was careless about dates.§他在注明出处上**一丝不苟**，在日期上却马虎。
scrutinize§Scrutinize the method before you admire the result.§在赞叹结果之前，先**审视**方法。
scrutiny§Under scrutiny the figure turned out to be an estimate.§一经**细查**，这个数字原来只是估算。
scuttle§A rumor scuttled the merger three days before signing.§一则谣言在签约前三天**毁掉**了这次合并。
seclude§A secluded corner of the garden was never photographed.§花园里一个**僻静**的角落从未被拍下来。
seclusion§Seclusion is a working condition, not a personality.§**隐居**是一种工作条件，而不是一种性格。
secrecy§Secrecy about a good result is usually about the funding.§对好结果**保密**，通常是为了资金。
secretive§Glands in the leaf are secretive and produce a sticky resin.§叶片上的腺体具**分泌**功能，会产生黏性树脂。
sedate§They sedated the animal for a ten-minute examination.§他们给这只动物用了**镇静**剂，做了十分钟检查。
sedentary§Sedentary birds here do not migrate at all.§这里的**留鸟**完全不迁徙。
seditious§Seditious libel was the charge and the pamphlet was the evidence.§罪名是**煽动性**诽谤，证据就是那本小册子。
sedulous§Sedulous attention to the index made the book usable.§对索引**一丝不苟**的用心让这本书变得好用。
seep§Doubt seeped into the argument somewhere in chapter four.§怀疑在第四章的某处**渗进**了论证。
self-centered§A self-centered account is still a first-hand one.§**以自我为中心**的叙述仍然是第一手的。
self-critical§Self-critical in private, he defended the work in public.§他私下**自我批评**，公开场合却为作品辩护。
self-destructive§A self-destructive habit is easier to name than to change.§**自毁的**习惯说出来容易，改起来难。
self-evaluation§Self-evaluation forms measure compliance, not performance.§**自我评价**表衡量的是配合度，而非表现。
selfishness§Selfishness at the top becomes policy at the bottom.§高层的**自私**到了基层就变成了政策。
self-serving§A self-serving account is not necessarily an untrue one.§**自利**的叙述未必是不真实的。
sensation§The book caused a sensation and was out of print in a year.§这本书**轰动一时**，一年内就绝版了。
sensational§A sensational find turned out to be a Victorian copy.§一件**轰动**的发现原来是维多利亚时代的仿制品。
sensationalism§Sensationalism is what fills the space where reporting used to be.§**哗众取宠**填满了从前属于报道的位置。
sensible§She was sensible of the risk and took it anyway.§她**清楚**这个风险，还是承担了。
sentimental§He kept the ticket for sentimental reasons and no others.§他留着那张票纯粹**出于感情**，别无其他。
sequence§The sequence of operations matters more than any single step.§操作的**顺序**比任何单一步骤都重要。
serendipity§Serendipity favours the person who is already looking.§**机缘**偏爱那些已经在找的人。
serene§A serene expression in the portrait hides a difficult year.§肖像里**平静**的表情掩藏着艰难的一年。
serenity§Serenity in a crisis is usually preparation, not temperament.§危机中的**从容**通常来自准备，而非性情。
sermonize§The chapter sermonizes when it should simply describe.§这一章本该只作描述，却变成了**说教**。
serpentine§The argument is serpentine and arrives somewhere worth being.§这个论证**蜿蜒**曲折，最后到达了一个值得抵达的地方。
servile§Servile imitation of a good model produces a bad copy.§对好范本的**奴性模仿**只会产出糟糕的复制品。
servility§Servility and loyalty are told apart by what happens when you disagree.§**奴性**与忠诚的区别，在于你提出异议时会发生什么。
setback§Treat a setback as data and it stops being a defeat.§把**挫折**当作数据，它就不再是失败。
severe§A severe editor is a gift you recognize ten years later.§**严厉的**编辑是一份十年后才认得出的礼物。
shopworn§Shopworn phrases survive because they are easy to type.§**陈旧**的套话之所以留存，是因为它们打起来省事。
showy§A showy demonstration proved less than a quiet measurement.§一次**炫目**的演示证明的东西，不如一次安静的测量。
shrewd§A shrewd reader checks the dates before the argument.§**精明的**读者会先核对日期，再看论证。
shroud§The shroud of secrecy was mostly incompetence.§那层保密的**帷幕**大半是无能。
shyness§Shyness in a lecture hall and confidence on the page often coexist.§讲台上的**羞怯**与纸面上的自信常常并存。
significant§A significant date in the margin dated the whole manuscript.§页边一个**重要的**日期确定了整份手稿的年代。
similarity§Similarity is not evidence of contact.§**相似**不能证明有过接触。
simplicity§Simplicity at the end of a project is expensive.§项目末期的**简洁**是昂贵的。
simplification§A simplification is honest only if it is labeled as one.§**简化**只有在被标明为简化时才是诚实的。
simplistic§Do not call an argument simplistic when you mean short.§想说“短”的时候，别说人家“过分**简单化**”。
sincerity§Sincerity is not a defence against being wrong.§**真诚**不能作为出错的辩护。
singularly§He was singularly unsuited to the job and did it for years.§他**极其**不适合这份工作，却做了很多年。
situate§Situate the finding in its period before you judge it.§在评判之前，先把这个发现**放回它的时代**。
skeptic§A skeptic and a cynic ask different questions.§**怀疑者**与愤世者问的是不同的问题。
skepticism§Skepticism is a method; suspicion is a mood.§**怀疑**是一种方法，猜忌是一种情绪。
slapstick§Slapstick survives translation better than wordplay.§**闹剧**比文字游戏更经得起翻译。
slender§A slender volume of forty pages outsold everything else.§一本四十页的**小册子**销量超过了其他所有书。
slipshod§Slipshod work by one person costs six people a week.§一个人的**马虎**让六个人损失一周。
slovenly§Slovenly notes are worse than no notes at all.§**潦草**的笔记比没有笔记更糟。
smug§There is nothing smug about being carefully right.§审慎地正确并不**自以为是**。
sneer§A sneer in print is permanent and rarely worth it.§印在纸上的**讥笑**是永久的，很少值得。
